Preconditions: No lead capture config exists; User has admin access
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to Settings > Lead Capture
2. Confirm no configuration exists
3. Click Create Default Configuration
4. Observe result
Expected Result: Default configuration created; Name, Email, Phone fields pre-populated; Save Configuration button available

Preconditions: Lead capture config exists with name and email fields
Test Steps:
1. Go to Settings > Lead Capture
2. Verify name and email fields present
3. Click Save Configuration
4. Observe confirmation
Expected Result: Configuration saves successfully; Success message displayed; Config persists on refresh

Test Steps:
1. Go to Settings > Lead Capture
2. Remove the name field
3. Attempt to click Save Configuration
4. Observe validation
Expected Result: Save is blocked; Validation error shown; Configuration not persisted

Test Steps:
1. Go to Settings > Lead Capture
2. Add new field type Dropdown
3. Enter comma-separated options e.g. Sales, Support, General
4. Save Configuration
Expected Result: New dropdown field appears; Options stored correctly; Field appears in collection flow when triggered

Test Steps:
1. Go to Settings > Lead Capture
2. Use arrows to reorder fields
3. Save Configuration
4. Trigger a lead capture conversation
Expected Result: Fields display in new order in settings; Bot asks questions in reordered sequence

Preconditions: Lead capture configured; Trigger phrase: contact me about your services
Test Steps:
1. Open chatbot
2. Type: I'd like someone to get in touch with me
3. Observe bot response
Expected Result: Lead capture flow activates via semantic matching; Bot transitions into collection flow; First field requested

Preconditions: Lead capture configured; Trigger keyword: pricing
Test Steps:
1. Open chatbot
2. Type: Can you send me pricing info?
3. Observe bot response
Expected Result: Lead capture flow activates; Bot begins collecting lead fields

Preconditions: Lead capture configured with specific triggers
Test Steps:
1. Open chatbot
2. Type: What are your business hours?
3. Observe bot response
Expected Result: Lead capture flow does NOT activate; Bot responds normally

Test Case: No Triggers Configured — Manual Start Only
Preconditions: Lead capture configured with no triggers
Test Steps:
1. Open chatbot
2. Type various messages
3. Observe that auto-trigger never fires
Expected Result: Lead capture does not auto-start; Flow only starts manually

Preconditions: Config with Name, Email, Phone fields; Trigger phrase active
Test Steps:
1. Type trigger phrase in chatbot
2. Respond: Name: Sarah Chen, Email: sarah@example.com, Phone: +61 412 345 678
3. Observe final message
Expected Result: Bot asks each field in configured order; Consent text displayed; Thank you message shown; Conversation continues normally

Test Steps:
1. Trigger lead capture flow
2. When bot asks for email, type: skip
3. Observe bot behaviour
Expected Result: Bot re-prompts for required field; Flow does not advance until required field provided

Preconditions: Config with at least one non-required field
Test Steps:
1. Trigger lead capture
2. When optional field prompted, type: skip
3. Observe flow progression
Expected Result: Bot accepts the skip; Flow continues to next field; Lead captured without optional value

Test Steps:
1. Trigger lead capture
2. Complete the collection flow
3. Observe when consent text appears
Expected Result: Consent text displayed during flow; Lead record shows consent given; Consent timestamp stored

Preconditions: Config includes Dropdown field with options: Sales, Support, General
Test Steps:
1. Trigger lead capture
2. When dropdown field prompted, provide a valid option
3. Observe lead record
Expected Result: Bot presents available options; Selected option stored correctly in lead record

Test Steps:

2. Navigate to Leads in sidebar
3. Observe lead list
Expected Result: New lead appears; Status is New; Name, Email, Phone, Source, Created date correct

Preconditions: Multiple leads exist across different statuses
Test Steps:

2. Observe: Total, New, Qualified, Converted stat cards
Expected Result: Each card count matches filtered table count; Total matches sum of all leads

Test Steps:

2. Enter a partial name in search box
3. Observe table results
Expected Result: Table filters to show only matching leads; Matches by name, email, phone or company

Test Steps:

2. Select Qualified from status filter
3. Observe table
Expected Result: Only Qualified leads displayed; Count matches Qualified stat card

Test Steps:

2. Click a lead row or eye icon
3. Observe detail page
Expected Result: Lead detail opens; Contact info, status, notes, assigned-to visible; Custom fields and consent details displayed

Test Steps:

2. Change Status to Contacted
3. Click Save Changes
4. Refresh and re-open lead
Expected Result: Status updates to Contacted; Change persists after refresh; Leads table reflects updated status

Test Steps:

4. Refresh page
Expected Result: Notes saved and displayed on refresh; Notes content preserved exactly

Test Steps:

Expected Result: Assignment saved; Assigned user shown on lead detail and in table view

Test Steps:

Expected Result: Bot uses tone defined in lead capture system prompt; Distinct from main chatbot prompt

2. Click Templates in System Prompt section
3. Select a template
4. Observe field
